newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish police, protesters clash in Ankara.
newsitem.headline: Turkish police, protesters clash in Ankara.

text.p: Turkish police on Saturday used water cannons and batons to disperse thousands of public service workers marching in the capital Ankara for higher wages, television reported.
State-run Anatolian news agency said 33 protesters were taken into custody after people threw sticks and stones at police trying to search demonstrators.

The march through the capital was called by the Confederation of Public Workers Unions to stress demands for improved wages amid concern that economic conditions for workres will worsen under the 1997 budget. Parliament began debating the budget this week and is scheduled to finish on December 18.
Protesters also chanted calls for a "clean society", alluding to a scandal that has linked the Turkish state and police with a wanted criminal allegedly used to kill off political opponents.
Television pictures showed police attacking protesters with batons and Anatolian said the police fired shots into the air when the stone-throwing continued.
